akiec.name: Actinic Keratosis / Intraepithelial Carcinoma
akiec.description: Rough, scaly, or crusty skin patches caused by long-term sun exposure. Potential to develop into Squamous Cell Carcinoma if untreated.
akiec.immediate_advice: Schedule an appointment with a dermatologist for evaluation. Avoid sun exposure and use SPF 50+ sunscreen.

bcc.name: Basal Cell Carcinoma
bcc.description: The most common form of skin cancer. Arises in basal cells and typically presents as a pearly nodule, translucent bump, or non-healing sore.
symptoms: Sore that bleeds, oozes, or crusts
bcc.immediate_advice: Consult a board-certified dermatologist promptly. Basal cell carcinoma is highly treatable when caught early.

bkl.name: Benign Keratosis-like Lesion
bkl.description: Includes seborrheic keratoses and solar lentigines. Non-cancerous skin growths that often appear waxy, scaly, or slightly raised.
bkl.immediate_advice: These lesions are benign and usually do not require medical intervention unless inflamed or for cosmetic reasons.

df.name: Dermatofibroma
df.description: Common firm, harmless skin nodules, frequently found on lower legs. Usually dimple inward when pinched.
df.immediate_advice: Dermatofibromas are non-malignant. Monitor for any sudden changes in size, color, or shape.

mel.name: Melanoma
mel.description: The most serious type of skin cancer, developing in melanocytes. Follows the ABCDE criteria (Asymmetry, Border, Color, Diameter, Evolving).
mel.immediate_advice: URGENT: Schedule an immediate evaluation with an oncologist or dermatologist. Do not scratch or attempt self-treatment.

nv.name: Melanocytic Nevi (Common Mole)
nv.description: Common benign moles caused by clusters of melanocytes. Typically uniform in color, round or oval with smooth borders.
nv.immediate_advice: Perform routine monthly self-exams using the ABCDE guidelines. Consult a doctor if the mole evolves.

vasc.name: Vascular Lesion
vasc.description: Includes cherry angiomas, angiokeratomas, and vascular malformations originating from blood vessels.
vasc.immediate_advice: Generally benign. Seek medical review if the lesion bleeds frequently or rapidly expands.
